title: Research Sprint
summary: YTIntel can now take a niche from discovery to a ready-to-make video brief in one guided evidence-first workflow.
discord_changes: New Research Sprint chains Opportunity Radar, structured Pattern Mine validation and Packaging intelligence into one guided workflow.
The final output is a ready-to-make brief with title, thumbnail, opening hook, validated pattern, evidence level, risk and test plan.
Smart Start is now genuinely wired into production, with improved mobile navigation, PWA caching and full sprint backup/restore.
changes: Added Research Sprint as a new top-level guided workflow for creators who want an answer rather than a collection of separate reports.
A sprint begins with a niche or topic and automatically runs Opportunity Radar to discover and channel-verify candidate videos.
Research Sprint selects a 5–8 video evidence set, preferring a repeated cross-channel concept when one is strong enough and otherwise using a channel-diverse ranked set.
The sprint refuses to continue with fewer than five usable research videos.
The sprint also refuses to build a production recommendation unless the selected set contains at least two verified winners across at least two independent channels.
Pattern Mine now runs as structured data inside Research Sprint instead of being treated only as a separate visual report.
The structured Pattern Mine output is passed directly into Packaging intelligence together with the verified Radar winners, controls, clusters and research-set metadata.
This means the final title, thumbnail and opening-hook options can reason over cross-video repeated evidence and winner-vs-pack differences rather than only the initial discovery scan.
Added automatic YouTube thumbnail reconstruction from video IDs when discovery data does not preserve a thumbnail URL, improving multimodal packaging inputs.

Added a final Ready-to-Make Brief with the recommended title, concept, viewer promise, thumbnail direction, opening hook, cross-video pattern evidence, package/evidence/replication/novelty/clarity scores, risk, kill condition and test plan.
Ready-to-Make Briefs can be copied in one click or sent directly into Creator Loop as a planned production experiment.
Research Sprint sessions are saved locally and recent sprints can be reopened instead of being lost when the user navigates away.
Added clear Discover → Validate → Package → Ready progress states so users always know what YTIntel is doing and why.
Added explicit blocked states when evidence is too thin, rather than padding weak research into a confident-looking recommendation.
Added a Full Research Sprint action beside Smart Start for users who want the complete workflow rather than automatic routing into a single tool.
Actually wired the existing Smart Start runtime and stylesheet into the production HTML; the universal input is now part of the live application bootstrap.
Promoted Smart Start to the main entry point in the production shell while keeping all advanced research tools available.
Added Research Sprint to Quick Switch and made it a first-class navigation destination.
Updated mobile quick navigation to surface Start, Sprint, Analyse and Creator Loop as the four primary mobile actions.
Updated the installed-app shortcuts to include Research Sprint.
Updated the PWA runtime cache to v0.17.0 and included the Smart Start, Research Sprint, mobile navigation and current shell assets in the offline shell.
Removed the superseded broken first-pass sprint runtime before release.
Added Research Sprint history and the active sprint reference to full YTIntel backup/restore.
Kept the single-owner shell architecture so historical feature modules cannot overwrite the current browser title, status or What's New experience.
why_it_matters: YTIntel had enough individual research tools, but creators still had to know how to combine them. Research Sprint changes the product from a toolbox into a workflow: start with the niche you care about, let YTIntel discover and verify the market, validate the pattern across competitors, build an original execution from that evidence, and leave with a production brief that can move straight into Creator Loop. The sprint is intentionally allowed to stop when evidence is weak; the goal is useful decisions, not a confident answer at any cost.
